title: Expanded testing capacity bolsters drug enforcement and public safety
text:
At Thursday's weekly Cabinet meeting, Premier Cho Jung-tai received a Ministry of Justice (MOJ) report on expanding testing capacity for emerging drugs and urine samples. The premier said that the government introduced a range of measures centered on three policy fronts to address the rapid spread of etomidate and other emerging drugs: deterrence at the source, increased enforcement, and tougher penalties for drug-impaired driving. Recognizing that adequate testing capacity is critical to effective law enforcement, the Executive Yuan approved an initiative on September 1 to expand testing capacity for emerging drugs, thereby bolstering both frontline enforcement and laboratory testing capabilities.

To expand testing capacity, Premier Cho directed the MOJ and the Ministry of the Interior to expedite equipment installation and personnel deployment at central and local laboratories, with the aim of increasing testing capabilities for drug samples and urine specimens, reducing testing turnaround times and enhancing the effectiveness of law enforcement and judicial investigations.

The premier underscored that combating drugs and curbing drug-impaired driving are vital to maintaining public order and safety, and called on relevant ministries and agencies to continue working with local governments to demonstrate their collective resolve to tackle drugs and protect the public.
